events.summary:
A monthly meetup for Portland business owners who want AI to take real work off their plate. Practical, plain English, no sales pitch.

​The talk is built by you. When you RSVP, tell us what's eating your team's hours. We'll build a short talk around what registrants are struggling with.

​What to expect

​7:00 -- arrive, meet a few people

​7:15 -- a 15-20 minute talk built from your signup answers

​7:30 -- Q&A. Bring the specific problem

​7:50 -- networking, wrapping up by 8:30

​Who it's for: owners and operators of small and mid-sized businesses. No technical background needed. If your business runs on a spreadsheets only one person understands, you're in the right room.

​Free.
events.title: AI for Portland Business Owners

events.summary:
Join PDX Women Coders for a back-end study session, where we read and discuss Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd edition) (https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/designing-data-intensive-applications/9781098119058/) by Martin Kleppmann. We plan to go over one chapter (or so) each session, and we will be meeting every two weeks for 7-8 months to finish the book. Each session, we'll go over that we learned in that chapter, and explore key concepts in distributed systems, data storage, and scalable architecture. We hope this will be a good opportunity to learn and connect with fellow engineers.

Before our reboot* meeting, please read the first chapter.

Some additional details:
- We are meeting every two weeks @ 10AM PT on Zoom
- The Zoom event link willl be shared 2-3 days before the event
- Anyone can attend, regardless of gender, as long as you support our mission
- Reading is not required for attendance
(but you'll get more out of this session if you read along 😉)
- The event photo comes from Martin Kleppmann's blog post: Drawing a map of distributed data systems (https://martin.kleppmann.com/2017/03/15/map-distributed-data-systems.html)

*This event series was created and organized by Kat K. starting in February 2024. We read the first edition of the book back then; we will be reading the second edition this time around.
events.title: Backend & Systems Guild: Designing Data-Intensive Applications [Ch. 1]

events.summary:
Working with data that's too large, too slow, or too messy for regular CSVs? Join us for an introduction to the {arrow} package in R. We'll explore how Arrow and Parquet files can make large datasets faster to store, read, and analyze, all while using the familiar dplyr workflows you already know and love. Using Portland's Biketown data, we'll convert, query, and visualize millions of rides without breaking a sweat (or our laptops).

Bring your laptop if you want to follow along.

No need to RSVP via Meetup, but we might share info ahead of time in the event comments!
events.title: Big Data? No Problem! An introduction to arrow for R

Details
## What to Expect:
Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session. Drink some coffee, bring your laptop, and have engaging conversations. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work tasks.
Still uncertain? Let's chat on Discord!
## Venue:
The Venue is at Roseline Café, who is graciously allowing us to host a space. WIFI, power outlets
Recommended Parking: Smart Park, $7 all day https://www.portland.gov/transportation/parking/smartpark

## Coffee:
Roseline Café has drip coffee and fixings available for it

## Agenda:
10 AM - Arrival
10:15 AM - Introductions:
Share your name
Discuss your current projects or interests. If you don’t have a specific project, share what intrigues you!
Mention your expertise and how you can assist others.
Are you job hunting or hiring? Let us know!
Community events you wanna plug. If none, that's cool too.
12:30 AM - Wrapping Up: You can stay longer, but we'll officially be done! We usually grab lunch as a group at near by food carts
